# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

## Plan review — 2026-11-05 (verified state)

Verified against the current checkout: main-street `dev` at `f4f083ed`, `core` submodule pinned at `5a16c2fb`, superproject working tree clean.

- **AC1 met** — `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains `achievementId: serial-seller` with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false` (13 entries in total).
- **AC3 met** — the `core` pointer now pins `5a16c2fb`, later than the `d2d1f322` recorded above, and that commit contains the manifest entry.
- **AC4 preconditions satisfied** — the parent mapping (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J) is now **committed**, not uncommitted as stated above: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 13 challenges, and the manifest and the game-side mapping agree exactly (13 ↔ 13, no drift in either direction). `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` is the guard that exercises this.
- **AC2 unmet / external** — unchanged: blocked on `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (Steamworks backend registration). Not verifiable from the repository.
- **AC5** — no documentation change beyond the manifest entry was identified as required; the existing 12-achievement pattern is followed.
- **AC6** — enforced by the dev-push gate; not re-run by this planning session.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05 — Plan re-run (effort Extra Small / Low, so decomposition skipped): six review stages run, AC coverage 100% (proceed), stage set to `plan_complete`. Recorded the verified AC state above; no child work items created.

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).

- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /

  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated** (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing and end-of-turn summary sections, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,
  intake_complete) — ordering constraint.
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item (shared with
  single-player panel).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on Game Over; consumes the same per-turn ledger data
  (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's `closingSummary` / shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` + `MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0` (completed) — competitive
  per-seat income choreography and per-seat animated closing: the cadence this
  panel extends; `TurnResult.playerIncome` originates here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`
  reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (round = day):** "one panel per completed round" maps to one
  panel per completed shared day (every seat finished + closing ran); the
  engine has no separate round concept. Recorded from repo evidence; if a
  day-vs-round distinction exists conceptually (e.g. a preset defining round
  length), the panel cadence would need revisiting — flagged for implementer
  verification.
- **Assumption (single human seat):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one
  device, so a blocking dialog on the human's **[ Next Turn ]** cannot stall
  other humans; multifloored safety holds for the current product shape.
  (If networked multiplayer ever lands, blocking semantics need a per-seat
  pause protocol.)
- **Risk (parent not landed):** the owner-keyed ledger this item consumes does
  not exist yet; if the parent lands without the per-seat expense capture
  (today `void`/log-only), this item must extend it — keep additions optional
  and guarded so `presentCompetitiveClosing` and headless/Monte-Carlo flows are
  byte-stable when absent.
- **Risk (blocking regresses headless pacing):** the gate must live in the
  scene presentation tail only (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`), never in engine
  close functions; Monte-Carlo / AI headless days never touch the scene and
  must continue to auto-advance under `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
- **Risk (eliminated seats):** the closing already omits eliminated seats from
  `playerIncome`; the panel must render exactly the seats the closing surfaced
  (no ghost rows for bankrupt/eliminated seats) and say so in its test.
- **Risk (loans are per-owner):** the shared disabled Bank Loan seam is a
  single hook today; when MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands, competitive loans are
  likely per-seat — keep the seam shaped so it can become
  `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` without re-plumbing the panel.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-round history across days (post-game stats,
  MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), networked multiplayer, live loans
  (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) and any round-summary log/graph features are outside
  this item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Blocking behaviour — in single-player the dialog blocks the next-day
  advance until [ Next Turn ] is clicked; in competitive the day currently
  auto-advances after the closing presentation. Options: A) Block like
  single-player — next day starts only after [ Next Turn ]. B) Non-blocking —
  panel appears but the day advances behind it / auto-dismisses."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — consistency
  with the single-player dialog; accepted as chosen.)
- Q2: "Per-seat data source — per-seat expenses aren't captured anywhere
  today (TurnResult.playerIncome covers income only). Options: A) Extend the
  engine with an owner-keyed per-seat ledger on TurnResult (per-seat ongoing
  costs, businesses owned, net change — engine-computed, testable headless),

# Per-turn stat history capture and series model

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (tracer bullet, phase 1).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want my run's per-turn economy recorded and the
final **Cash at end of turn** shown in the Game Over Summary, so the run's
trajectory survives the run and can be charted in the next phase.

## Scope

- **In:** `TurnStatSnapshot` type + `turnStatsHistory` initialisation, capture
  on **every** end-of-turn closing path, save/load persistence with a legacy
  `[]` fallback, the pure `buildGameOverStatSeries` model, and the Summary
  column's cash-at-end-of-turn line.
- **Out:** graph/chart rendering (third-column child), competitive-mode series
  assertions, prose documentation (docs child). Inline JSDoc only here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn on the legacy and deferred paths, never twice.
2. **Snapshot shape and capture.** `TurnStatSnapshot { turn, coins,
   reputation, score, profit, businesses, staff }` is exported from
   `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, and `turnStatsHistory` is added to
   `MainStreetState` and initialised to `[]` by both `setupMainStreetGame` and
   `createCompetitiveState`; `profit = coins − (weekStartCoins ?? current
   coins)` (the `appendTurnNetRow` definition), `businesses` = non-null
   `streetGrid` entries, `staff = staffCards.length`. Capture lives in the
   shared closing tail so the legacy path (`runSinglePlayerTurnClosing`,
   including its immediate-loss early exit), the deferred path
   (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, including its immediate-loss early exit) and
   the competitive closing path each record exactly once; a repeat call for the
   same `turn` appends nothing; `npm run build` (tsc) is clean.
3. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState`.
4. **Persistence details.** It is restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`; a
   legacy save without the field loads with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data). Unit tests cover round-trip fidelity and the legacy
   fallback.
5. **Pure series model.** `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` in
   `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` returns the five series
   (profit, cash, businesses, staff, reputation at end of turn) as labelled
   point arrays plus `finalCash` (last recorded `coins`, falling back to
   `state.resourceBank.coins` for an empty history). No Phaser import; an empty
   history yields empty series and a valid `finalCash`. Unit tests cover a
   populated history, an empty history, and non-mutation of `state`.
6. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture on both paths and no
   double-record.
7. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established overlay
   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depth 201 and `overlayObjects`.
8. **Summary cash line.** `showGameOverOverlay` renders
   `Cash at end of turn: <n>` in the Summary column directly after the score
   breakdown, with no clipping and no change to existing Summary content, and
   reads committed state only (the snapshot is byte-identical before/after the
   call); an overlay unit test asserts the line renders and the existing
   content is retained.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory` on
   `MainStreetState` and `MainStreetSerializedState`.
2. `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — `turnStatsHistory: []` in both setups.
3. `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — record from the shared closing tail
   (`appendTurnNetRow`) via a small `recordTurnStats(state, turnEnded)` helper,
   keyed by `turn`.
4. `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise the array; restore with
   `saved.turnStatsHistory ?? []` (tolerate malformed entries defensively).
5. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverStatSeries`.
6. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Summary cash line.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — snapshot interface + state/serialized fields.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise `turnStatsHistory: []`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `recordTurnStats` called from the
  closing tail.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise/restore with legacy fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverStatSeries`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Summary cash line.
- `tests/main-street/turn-stats-history.test.ts` — **new** capture/persistence
  unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stat-series.test.ts` — **new** series-model
  unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` — extended cash-line assertion.

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the chart, third-column, competitive, docs and acceptance children.

## Deliverables

Code + unit tests + inline JSDoc, all green under the changed-scope test gate.

## Risks

- Deferred and legacy closing paths may record twice — mitigated by the
  `turn`-keyed guard and targeted tests.
- Competitive closing reuses the shared scratch bank; this child records what
  the closing tail sees and defers the seat-scope assertion to the competitive
  child.

# Chart library integration spike

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 2, risk burn-down).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer on Main Street, I want proven, isolated Chart.js integration
with the Phaser 4 canvas so the end-of-game graphs can be built on a known-good
foundation instead of during layout work.

## Context

Producer decision Q3 = **B**: use an external charting library (e.g. Chart.js)
rather than hand-rolled `Graphics` or SVG-as-texture. Chart.js needs a canvas
context and a DOM element, and it must never load or run in replay / headless
(Monte-Carlo) runs. This spike de-risks that integration before five graphs are
laid out.

## Scope

- **In:** dependency addition, a thin `MainStreetStatsChart.ts` wrapper, one
  working overlay chart, headless/replay skip, teardown, bundle-size evidence
  and a documented spike verdict.
- **Out:** the five real graphs and column layout (third-column child), styling
  polish, docs prose (docs child).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dependency.** The chosen charting library (Chart.js preferred) is added to
   `dependencies` in `package.json` with the lockfile updated; `npm run build`
   is clean; the production bundle-size delta (before/after, kB and gzip) is
   recorded in a work-item comment.
2. **Wrapper exists and is Phaser-thin.** `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts`
   exposes a create/destroy pair (e.g. `createStatsChart(scene, geometry, spec)`
   → handle, `destroyStatsChart(handle)`) that renders **one line chart** into a
   dedicated DOM `<canvas>` positioned over the Phaser canvas at the requested
   overlay coordinates; the module has no game-state imports and no Phaser
   scene mutation.
3. **Headless/replay safe.** `createStatsChart` returns `null` and creates no
   DOM node when `scene.replayMode` is true or when no DOM is available
   (`typeof document === 'undefined'`); a unit test with a mocked chart
   constructor asserts zero constructions and zero nodes in both cases.
4. **Lazy-loaded.** The library is imported via a dynamic `import()` from the
   overlay path so headless/Monte-Carlo/replay entry points never resolve it;
   the existing engine/headless unit tests pass unchanged (changed-scope gate).
5. **No animation, clean teardown.** Charts are created with
   `animation: false` and no rAF/tween loop (reduced-motion safe); destroying
   the overlay removes every chart canvas — a browser test opens and closes the
   overlay 20 times and asserts zero leftover chart canvases and no console
   errors.
6. **Verdict recorded.** A work-item comment states: library + version, bundle
   delta, layering/positioning approach, teardown evidence, and whether the
   spike meets its thresholds (chart visible above the overlay panel at
   1280×720; gzip delta ≤ 150 kB; no leaks). If a threshold fails, the comment
   records the alternative approach and the item stops for producer review
   instead of continuing to the third-column child.

## Minimal implementation

1. `package.json` — add the charting dependency.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — dynamic-import wrapper, skip guards,
   positioning over the Phaser canvas, `destroyStatsChart` teardown.
3. Temporary wiring in `showGameOverOverlay` to draw one series so the browser
   test can exercise the real path.
4. Tests: unit skip/no-leak test with a mocked library, browser open/close
   cycle test.
5. Bundle measurement + spike comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — charting dependency.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **new** wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — temporary single-chart wiring.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.test.ts` — **new** unit skip/no-leak tests.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser teardown
  test.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the capture/series-model child (needs `buildGameOverStatSeries`).
Blocks the third-column child.

## Deliverables

Dependency + wrapper + tests + spike verdict comment.

## Risks

- Chart.js may fight the Phaser canvas for pointer/depth ordering — the wrapper
  must own a separate DOM layer and stay non-interactive in this phase.
- Bundle growth — mitigated by the measured gzip threshold and dynamic import.

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 3, main deliverable).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player at game over, I want a third column of graphs showing
my profit, cash, businesses, staff and reputation turn by turn, plus a link
from the Summary to that detail, so I can see what worked and what did not.

- **In:** third column composition of five graphs, panel/column geometry
  rebalance to fit 1280×720, the Summary → stats affordance, overlay
  conventions.

1. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing the
   five end-of-game graphs.
2. **Graph details.** The column is headed `Stats`, sits to the right of
   `Summary`, and contains, in order: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of
   turn**, **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn** and
   **reputation at end of turn**, each chart fed from
   `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` with a visible axis/legend label. An overlay
   unit test (chart module mocked) asserts five chart specs with the expected
   series and titles.
3. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final cash and
   links the stats column.
4. **Link detail.** The affordance is a `[ View detailed stats ]` control that
   focuses the stats column without animation (static focus frame and/or depth
   raise), is keyboard-activatable via `setInteractive`, reads no mutable state,
   and leaves `state` unchanged when activated (unit test).

   recomputed so three columns fit inside the 1280×720 viewport with no

   breakdown, challenge details, tier/campaign, difficulty, buttons) is
   retained; an overlay unit test asserts the geometry for a rich history
   (≥ 12 turns) and an empty history.

   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201 and
   `overlayObjects`.

   `scene.replayMode` early return; no tweens, rAF or other animation is added
   by the new column (reduced-motion safe); the overlay remains a read-only
   view of committed state.

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 4).

## Goal (user story)

As a competitive Main Street player, I want the same end-of-game graphs for my
own seat so a loss against the AI can be diagnosed, and I want the overlay to
fit the viewport in both game modes.

## Scope

- **In:** competitive-series scope, both-mode rendering/fit verification,
  replay/headless guard verification, reduced-motion confirmation.
- **Out:** per-seat multi-series graphs (only if the producer overrides the
  recorded working assumption — that would be a separate item), docs prose.

## Working assumption (plan Open Question)

Competitive mode plots the **human seat's** trajectory only (see the parent's
Appendix "OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope)"). This child asserts
and documents that assumption; it must not expand to per-seat series without
producer confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive series.** With a competitive fixture (`players[]` populated),
   the rendered series equal the recorded `turnStatsHistory` for the human
   seat's closing values, and no AI seat's wallet leaks into the series (unit
   test asserting series points against a hand-built competitive history).
2. **Human-seat recording.** The competitive closing path records one history
   entry per turn from the seat-scoped closing wallet (`findHumanSeatId`
   semantics), never one entry per AI seat; a unit test drives a scripted
   competitive turn and asserts exactly one entry with the human seat's coins.
3. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive modes and fits the 1280×720 layout.
4. **Both-mode render detail.** Browser tests assert the `Stats` column header,
   five chart canvases and the `Cash at end of turn` line render in
   **single-player** and **competitive** states, and that the panel stays
   inside 1280×720 with no clipping or vertical overflow in both.
5. **Replay/headless guard.** In `scene.replayMode` the overlay creates no
   chart canvas and no DOM node (unit test with a mocked scene asserting zero
   chart constructions), and headless Monte-Carlo/engine runs are unaffected
   (changed-scope tests green).
6. **Static, no animation.** No tweens or rAF are added by this child; the
   overlay is static so reduced-motion users see the same content.
7. **Scope discipline.** Any competitive-scope gap beyond the working
   assumption is recorded as an Open Question comment on the parent rather than
   implemented here.

# Colour of service businesses

## Problem statement

Service businesses render in a dark purple that is visually indistinguishable
from the flat purple face used by every upgrade card, so the two card families
read as the same thing at a glance on the street and in hand. At the same
time, an upgrade card carries no information about *what* it upgrades: all 39
upgrade cards share one uniform purple face regardless of the business they
apply to.

## Users

- **Main Street player** (primary) — scanning their hand and the market needs
  to distinguish a service business from an upgrade card instantly, and to see
  which family of business an upgrade belongs to without reading its title.
  - *As a player, I want service businesses in a colour no other card family
    uses, so I never mistake a service business for an upgrade card.*
  - *As a player, I want each upgrade card to show the colour of the business
    family it upgrades, so I can pick a relevant upgrade from my hand without
    reading every title.*

- **Colour-blind player** — the distinction must not rely on hue alone; the
  checkered pattern is itself a non-colour cue, and the upgrade card keeps its
  title and "for <Business>" target text.

## Existing state

- Synergy-type card faces are coloured from two parallel palettes:
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE` (dark faces, `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and the
  bright `synergyColor` accent palette. The static Node generator
  (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) duplicates both; an
  existing test asserts the two copies of the face palette agree
  (MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4).
- Service currently holds dark purple `#6A1B9A` (face) / `0x9B59B6` (accent).
- Upgrade cards are flat purple: background `#6B4C9A`, accent `#9B59B6`,
  rendered by `generateUpgradeCardSvg` / `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and by
  `cardColorScheme` / the family branch in the `.mjs` generator.
- 39 upgrade rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry a `targetBusiness` name but no
  synergy column of their own; synergy must be resolved by looking the target
  name up among business **and** community-space rows (6 targets are community
  spaces: Community Garden, Health Kiosk, Library, Park, Playground, Town
  Fountain).
- 9 businesses are bridge cards with two synergy types; 11 upgrade rows target
  them (Cafe, Food Truck, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga
  Studio, Teahouse).

## Desired change

1. **New service colour.** Replace Service's palette entries with a pink /
   magenta that no other synergy type uses, in **both** palettes (face and
   accent) and in **both** copies (TypeScript and the `.mjs` duplicate), so the
   palette-agreement test still passes.
2. **Checkered upgrade faces.** Upgrade card faces become a checkerboard of
   violet and the synergy colour of the business the upgrade targets, instead
   of the current flat purple.
3. **Bridge targets use both colours.** When the upgrade targets a card with
   two synergy types, the checkerboard uses both synergy colours (with violet
   in the remaining squares).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Service synergy type's face colour is a pink/magenta distinct from

# Engine DEVELOPER.md lists reduced motion among the paths that omit deferResourceApplication

Discovered from: MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X (Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting).

## Problem

`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the Tableau-Card-Engine submodule), section *Deferred End-of-Turn Mutation* → bullet *Deferred `processEndOfTurn`*, says:

> Tutorial, reduced-motion and replay paths omit the flag (legacy immediate behaviour, no regression — AC5).

After MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X the reduced-motion path does **not** omit the flag: the scene (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`) takes the deferred closing path under reduced motion, so the Turn Summary dialog has a `requiresDeferredClosing` result to gate on. Only the tutorial and replay paths still omit it.

## Why it was not fixed in the MS session

- `core` is a git submodule (a separate repository, detached HEAD at the engine pin `5a16c2f`). A working-tree edit leaves the submodule dirty, and `npm run build` runs `engine:sync` (non-soft), which **refuses** to sync a dirty submodule ("never clobber") — every later build in this repo would fail.
- A local commit inside the submodule is discarded by the next `engine:sync` (it checks out the remote target), so the fix would silently vanish.
- The engine checkout has no worklog (`wl` there reports "not initialized"), and pushing to the engine repo's `dev` is not authorised from a game-repo session.

## Fix

In the Tableau-Card-Engine repository, amend that bullet so only the tutorial and replay paths are named as flag-omitting, and state that the reduced-motion path takes the deferred closing so a game's Turn Summary gate can present its summary dialog (cross-reference the game-side behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer claims the reduced-motion path omits `deferResourceApplication`.
2. The bullet names the tutorial and replay paths as the immediate/flag-omitting ones and explains why the reduced-motion path is deferred.
3. No code change is required; the engine's documentation guards (if any) still pass.

# Intake Brief — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT)

## Problem statement

Specialization skills are assigned from a global 16-skill pool regardless of a staff card's type, and the street-wide folds aggregate every employed member's skills. As a result, a **business-staff** member can hold a **management-company-scope** skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, the four incident-mitigation skills, the Town Gossip baseline) and leak a player/street-scope effect, while a **management-company** member can draw **business-scope** skills (Chef, DJ, Networker, …) that can never resolve. The shipped behaviour therefore contradicts the two-type model reconciled in `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` (and GDD D.4.8), where a skill takes effect only from a member whose type matches the skill's scope.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — needs specialization skills to be a meaningful, type-consistent hiring signal: a business-staff hire improves its business, a management-company hire improves the player's turn, never an unexplained cross-scope leak.
- **Game designer / balance owner** — needs the shipped behaviour to match the documented two-type model so balance tuning and the skill catalog are trustworthy.
- **Implementing developer** — needs a deterministic, testable gate that preserves seeded reproducibility and existing save compatibility.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a skill held by a business-staff member to affect only that business, so that hiring decisions match the two-type model.
- As a game designer, I want assignment to draw skills consistent with a staff card's type, so that no card can hold an effect it can never realise.
- As a developer, I want the seeded assignment stream to stay deterministic, so that same seed ⇒ same game is preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope gate (behavioural).** A business-staff member holding a management-company-scope skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, any of the four incident-mitigation skills, or the Town Gossip baseline) produces **no** player- or street-scope effect; equally, a management-company member holding a business-scope skill produces **no** per-business buff. The Operations Manager salary discount remains a business-staff effect applied to its employing member.
2. **Type-consistent assignment (deterministic).** Business staff draw only business-scope skills; management-company staff draw only player-scope skills plus the Town Gossip baseline. The stacking caps (≤1 income-boost, ≤1 reputation-boost beyond baseline) remain per-member and type-neutral.
3. **Determinism preserved.** The assignment stream stays seeded and reproducible (same seed ⇒ same assignments); existing determinism tests continue to pass, and new determinism tests cover the type-consistent draw.
4. **Documentation updated.** `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` records that the follow-up gap is closed (or removes the follow-up section), and the GDD D.4.8 / `card-catalog.md` cross-references stay consistent. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Validation.** At least one automated test proves the scope gate (both leak directions) and the type-consistent assignment; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve determinism.** The assignment RNG stays the dedicated `createSeededRng(numericSeed ^ 0x5eed)` stream; do not perturb the main RNG stream (deck shuffles, market draws, challenges).
- **Preserve save compatibility.** Skills persist as stable id arrays; the staff type is derived from `employedAtSlot` and must not require a new stored field.
- **No new skills or magnitude changes.** The 16-skill catalog and its magnitudes are unchanged; this item only gates effects and constrains assignment.
- **Two staff types only.** Business staff = has `employedAtSlot`; management-company staff = no `employedAtSlot` (GDD D.4.2/D.4.8). No third type or skill flag.
- **Documentation-only gap closure.** Update the follow-up section of `specialization-skills.md` to mark the gap closed; do not re-open the two-type design.
- **UK English** throughout.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — `STAFF_SKILL_CATALOG` (16 skills, 4 categories); `assignSkillsToApplicant(rng)` draws from the **global** pool and always adds the Town Gossip baseline; `assignStaffApplicantSkills(state)` seeds assignments across the staff deck and market row. The catalog carries no scope/type field today.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` flattens **every** employed member's skills (street-wide); `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness(state, slot)` flattens only that slot's members; `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`, `computeIncidentSkillBuffs`, `computeStreetOngoingCostReductionPct`, `computeRefreshCostDiscount`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `computeReputationGainMultiplier`, etc. translate skills to effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — consume the street-wide and per-business aggregations.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — § *Shipped cross-type assignments — reconciliation follow-up* documents the two gaps and states they are not yet fixed; the skill table already classifies 8 business-staff and 8 management-company skills.
- Existing tests: `staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts` (determinism, stacking, baseline), `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `specialization-skills-two-types.test.ts` (doc contract).

## Desired change

1. **Scope gate.** Make street-wide/player-scope effect folds read only management-company members' skills, and per-business folds read only business-scope skills from the employing business's members — so a skill is inert when its scope does not match its holder's type. Keep the Operations Manager salary discount as a business-staff effect.
2. **Type-consistent assignment.** Draw business-scope skills for business staff and player-scope skills for management-company staff, always keeping the Town Gossip baseline on management-company cards. Preserve the per-member stacking caps and the seeded, reproducible stream.
3. **Docs + tests.** Update the `specialization-skills.md` follow-up section (gap closed/removed) and GDD/card-catalog cross-references; add determinism and scope-gate tests.

- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — scope-gated `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` / `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness`; per-business fold gating.

- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.8) / `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — cross-reference consistency.
- `tests/main-street/staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts` — scope-gate and determinism coverage.

- **MS-0MW2XMB0P002D95K** — Reconcile specialization-skills.md with the two-type model (completed; discovered this item). Explicitly deferred the behavioural/assignment gaps.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — determinism regression:** changing the candidate pool per type alters the seeded stream; *mitigation:* dedicated tests assert same-seed reproducibility across both types, and the salt/main-stream separation is preserved.
- **Risk — partial gate:** gating only the assignment leaves a stale save or hand-built fixture with a cross-type skill leaking; *mitigation:* the scope gate is enforced at the aggregation site, not only at assignment, and tests cover a cross-type skill held by both staff types.

The discovering item MS-0MW2XMB0P002D95K already recorded the two gaps and the producer-approved two-type model, so the intake proceeds without an interview.
